blocks.content: Avoiding exam traps is not just about knowledge, but about strategy, speed, and careful question reading.

rows: Check for valid exceptions before selecting the option
Rephrase the question into a positive statement before answering
Overly convoluted text or multi-step calculation
Skip immediately and attempt only if time permits at the end

items: Always circle keywords like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', or 'EXCEPT' before reviewing response options.
Watch out for options containing correct numeric values paired with incorrect units of measurement.
Never spend more than 60-90 seconds on a single complex trap during your first pass through the paper.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Exam traps are deliberately crafted by paper setters to trigger negative marking and consume excess time.
Extreme keywords such as 'always', 'never', and 'completely' frequently signal false statements in multiple-choice questions.
Question phrasing containing 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', or 'EXCEPT' causes the highest rate of avoidable errors.
Effective exam strategy requires skipping time-sink traps during the initial question sweep.
